request.spec:
The audit viewer, filtered by a name, now also lists the matching lines of the sheet's descendants
(each sheet's lines newest first, sheets by id, after this sheet's own lines and before the lines
from the sheet a person came from).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The audit viewer, filtered by a name, now also lists the matching lines of the sheet's descendants
(each sheet's lines newest first, sheets by id, after this sheet's own lines and before the lines
from the sheet a person came from).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
When the audit viewer is filtered by a name, it now also lists the matching lines from the sheet's descendants. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The change is in one file, `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/audit/RespondWithAuditLines.java`:
- **Which sheets count as descendants:** the code reuses the existing `Settings.family` method, which collects the sheets below this one by `parent`: its children, their children, and so on. It handles loops in the parent links.
- **Order:** this sheet's own lines come first, then each descendant's lines sorted by sheet id, each sheet's lines newest first. The lines from the sheet a person came from still come last.
- **Unchanged:** with no name filter, the viewer still shows only this sheet's own lines. No front-end, database or audit-record changes were needed.

One untested case: if the sheet a person came from is also one of this sheet's descendants, that sheet's lines will appear twice.
